outlook: Wheat led a mixed close Thursday, bouncing after Wednesday's dollar-driven selloff to eight-month lows: Minneapolis December spring wheat finished up 13 cents near $6.42 and Chicago December up about 8 cents near $5.78, helped by weekly wheat export sales of 345,000 tonnes (up 89%) and a Ukrainian ministry warning that its 2027 wheat crop could fall about a third to 17 million tonnes. December corn closed up 3.5 cents at $4.39 after Wednesday's 4.5-month low, with weekly export sales of 1.59 million tonnes in line with expectations. January soybeans slipped about 9.5 cents to near $12.07 despite strong weekly sales of 1.5 million tonnes, as Brazil rains support a record crop outlook and traders wait for any farm-purchase news from the Trump–Xi meeting at APEC. ICE January canola closed up C$5.50 at C$776.70 per tonne, while the U.S. dollar index stays near a 19-month high.
